matureFir.subject: Mature fir representative; not a taxonomically verified Japanese hemlock or cypress
processing: Extracted only variant C through HTTP Range; response206, exactContent-Range and length checked.
Attribute-aware mesh simplification preserving existing normals and UVs; full detail source retained in partial binary.
Removed constant white COLOR_0 and unreferenced COLOR_1 channels.
Restored cylindrical bark UVs on trunk primitive because original glTF had no TEXCOORD_0. Same-source bark texture used; UV seam split.

selection.definition: Outside the local rectangle, nearest study sample must have study-jogan=1 and study-landcover in [1,2,3]. Inside local x/z ±1024 m, use exact existing local forest instances, preserving forested local classes regardless of Jogan mask.
selection.interpretation: PROJECT INTERPRETATION: mapped eruption-product footprint intersected with forested landcover plus forested local core; not a legal, surveyed or definitive Aokigahara forest boundary.
selection.areaBasis: Exact clipped nearest-sample raster-cell area for the supplied categorical grids. Boundary sample cells extend half a cell inward. Study/local overlap is replaced, not double counted. This is a project mask area, not measured forest extent.

placement.roadSource: study-context.json OSM mapped centre lines; estimated exclusion widths include private/no-access tagged paths to match root exclusion rule

localOverlap.remainingRecords: All appended records are outside abs(x)<=1024 AND abs(z)<=1024; local and appended records never overlap.
localOverlap.use: Use this file to replace forest-instances.f32, or append only records after localPrefixCount to existing local instances. Do not append the complete file to the existing local instances.

productionPass2.summary: Production pass 2: near-field ground system, tree library v2, stand densification, deadwood/rock/fern layers, lighting presets. Coordinate framework, terrain grids, mapped paths, vegetation classes and the 53,999 corridor placements are unchanged; placements are re-used with deterministic per-instance size/form/tilt augmentation.

OBSERVED / SOURCE-CONSTRAINED: MOE community classes driving conifer/broadleaf/plantation variant mix (unchanged)
OSM path centre lines (unchanged); road vs trail class sets the base width only
IMG-013 published camera geotag used as an audit viewpoint (35.479278 N, 138.656892 E, heading 271.6°; precision uncalibrated)
INFERRED: Conifer-dominated stand with Tsuga-like and Chamaecyparis-like forms, dense small-stem regeneration, low gap fraction, exposed surface roots on thin soil over lava, moss on trunk bases/roots/rocks, litter collecting between roots and in hollows, fallen timber (ECO-001, ECO-002, IMG-007/008/013, ECO-016, GEO-002, ECO-029)
Path appearance: compacted dark cinder/soil with irregular edges, root and stone intrusion, litter at margins (route photographs; widths not measured)
PROCEDURAL: Lava micro-relief: metre-scale lobes/hummocks, 1–3 m block relief, sub-metre clinker, occasional linear clefts (amplitude ±0.6 m). Not surveyed; DEM cannot resolve it
Root mounds under each stem (Gaussian, 0.24 m × instance scale)
Moss / basalt / litter / trail layer weights from slope, curvature, noise, mound and path proximity
All textures in assets/materials_v2 (moss, basalt, litter, trail, blend noise); basalt reuses Poly Haven rock_3 relief (CC0)

Tree library v2: every trunk, buttress, surface root, branch and foliage card; species-suggestive only. Foliage cards cut from Poly Haven fir_tree_01 twig atlas (CC0) with alpha boosted; fir sprays stand in for Tsuga/Chamaecyparis sprays

Per-instance augmentation: size class (22% small, 66% mid, 12% dominant), 6% standing dead stems, ±2.6° tilt, variant by community class (class 1: 52% Tsuga-like / 48% hinoki-like; class 2: 50% broadleaf; class 3: hinoki-weighted)
Small stems (1.5–6 m) and sub-canopy stems (6–12 m) inserted in gaps with clustered density noise; radii 110–130 m and 170–230 m by quality setting
Lava blocks (5 noise-displaced icosahedra), embedded stones, fern instances (Poly Haven fern_02), fallen logs (Poly Haven dead_tree_trunk with procedural moss overlay)
Daylight presets (overcast reference / soft sun / clear) are adjustable visual states, not dated weather
UNKNOWN: Exact individual-tree positions, sizes and species; exact lava block and root arrangements; cave mouths/interiors; current signs, barriers and walkways; moss species composition and seasonal state

runtimeHierarchy.nearField: <46 m (balanced) / <62 m (high): tree-library-v2 high LOD (8–12k tris with roots and dense spray cards), 120 m relief ground patch at 0.6 m sampling, shadows from crowns
runtimeHierarchy.midField: to 230 m: low LOD (0.5–0.9k tris incl. crown-mass cards), sub-canopy stems, small stems to 110–130 m
runtimeHierarchy.regional: existing surface terrain GLB, base ground layers, lakes

notClaimed: Photorealism is not claimed; the pass narrows the gap. See renders/ for identical-camera before/after evidence.

No FPS figures for the target M2 MacBook Air were measured (not available in this session). Measured only: triangle counts per frame from the headless audit renderer (5.2–7.0 M triangles, 80–95 draw calls).

materialsV2Manifest.status: PROCEDURAL representatives. Not captured at Aokigahara. Derived inputs: Poly Haven rock_3 (CC0) relief/roughness reused inside basalt maps; everything else synthesised.
evidence_basis: GEO-002: Jogan products include aa and pahoehoe surfaces (blocky clinker and ropy folds)
IMG-007/008/013, ECO-016: moss carpets of varying thickness over irregular lava, roots gripping rock, litter collecting between roots
materialsV2Manifest.not_claimed: Moss species, exact colours, litter composition and lava micro-form are interpretive.

treeLibraryV2Manifest.provenance:
Aokigahara tree library v2 — deterministic procedural conifers with exposed surface-root systems.

Species-suggestive variants (NOT botanically exact, NOT surveyed individuals):
  tsuga   : Tsuga-like hemlock; grey plated bark (Poly Haven fir_tree_01 bark, CC0), spreading/drooping laterals, dark blue-green sprays
  hinoki  : Chamaecyparis-like cypress; reddish stringy bark (Poly Haven japanese_cedar_bark, CC0), ascending laterals, yellow-green sprays
  snag    : dead standing hemlock-type stem, broken top, bare branches (dead_tree_trunk textures, CC0)
  sapling : small hinoki/tsuga regeneration stems 1.5–6 m
Foliage cards use the Poly Haven fir_tree_01 twig atlas (CC0). Fir sprays are a REPRESENTATIVE stand-in for Tsuga/Chamaecyparis sprays.
Evidence basis for form: ECO-001/ECO-002 (Tsuga/hinoki stand, heterogeneous size classes, closed canopy, small gaps),
IMG-007/008/013 & ECO-016 (surface roots spreading over lava, moss on roots and trunk bases, leaning trunks).
Output: viewer/assets/tree-library-v2.glb  with meshes  <variant>_<lod>  lod in {high, low, far}.
Y up, metres, trunk base at y=0. Deterministic seeds.
